title: A rare case of bilateral en plaque meningioma presenting as a bilateral exophthalmos. A case report
case_prompt:
A 66-year-old woman presented with several months of progressive bilateral proptosis, decreased visual acuity, retrobulbar pressure, orbital pain, temporal-region swelling, and headaches. On evaluation in the emergency department, she was hemodynamically stable and neurologically intact. Ophthalmologic examination confirmed reduced visual acuity and more pronounced right-sided exophthalmos. Brain MRI demonstrated:
• Bilateral hyperostotic changes of the greater wings of the sphenoid bone, hypointense on both T1- and T2-weighted sequences.  
• Bilateral dural thickening and enhancement in the anterior temporal regions, invading the cavernous sinuses, prechiasmatic optic nerves, and lateral rectus muscles via the superior orbital fissures, with more marked involvement on the right.  
• Postcontrast sagittal images showed thickening and enhancement of the free border of the tentorium cerebelli and the retroclival dura.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Paget’s disease — “Given the bone involvement, our initial differential diagnosis encompassed Paget’s disease and fibrous dysplasia.”  
2. Fibrous dysplasia — “Given the bone involvement, our initial differential diagnosis encompassed Paget’s disease and fibrous dysplasia.”  
3. Primary intraosseous meningioma — “Hyperostoses observed in EPMs are characterized by surface irregularities and inward bulges of the affected structures. These subtle features aid in distinguishing hyperostosis from other conditions such as primary intraosseous meningioma…”
